chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of God, I am eager for jihad and energetic.' He said: 'Then fight in the way of God, for if you are killed, you will be alive with God receiving sustenance; if you die naturally, your reward is established with God; and if you return, you will emerge from sins as if you were just born.'

The man said: 'O Messenger of God, I have two elderly parents who say they find companionship through me and dislike my departure.' The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Stay with your parents, for by the One in whose hand is my soul, comforting them for a day and a night is better than a year of fighting.'

key_terms.أنسهما: Comforting/companionship with them — the emotional support children provide to elderly parents
key_terms.الجهاد: Jihad — striving or fighting in the way of God
key_terms.سبيل الله: The way of God — the path of righteous struggle

ai.seo_question: Does caring for elderly parents take priority over jihad in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) taught that while jihad has great merit in three outcomes — martyrdom, natural death, or safe return — the duty to elderly parents takes absolute precedence. When a young man expressed eagerness for battle but mentioned his elderly parents' dependence on him, the Prophet swore an oath that one day and night of comforting one's parents is better than an entire year of military campaign. This reflects the Quranic emphasis on kindness to parents (17:23).

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. `Abdullah b. Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from his grandfather Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah from his father from Ahmad b. al-Nadr al-Khazzaz from `Amr b. Shimr from Jabir b. Yazid al-Ju`fi from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah (s) and said: O Messenger of Allah! I want to fight, and I am fit. He said: Then fight in the way of Allah, for surely, if you are killed, you will be alive with Allah being given sustenance, and if you die [naturally], your reward will be with Allah, and if you return, your sins will be expunged as though you were just born.

So, he said: O Messenger of Allah! I have two elderly parents who say that they find harmony through me and hate for me to go out [to fight]. So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: Stay with your parents, for by He in whose hand is my soul, giving them harmony for a day and a night is better than a year of fighting.
